newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: SOCCER-EL SALVADOR RAISE WORLD CUP HOPES WITH 2-1 WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EL SALVADOR RAISE WORLD CUP HOPES WITH 2-1 WIN.

text.p: El Salvador brought themselves into contention for a place at the World Cup finals by beating Costa Rica 2-1 in the final round of the CONCACAF qualifying competition on Sunday.
Raul Diaz Arce struck the first blow for El Salvador in the 19th minute after Costa Rica, who beat the United States 3-2 in their last game, had dominated the early stages.
Midfielder Mauricio Solis hit the post in the ninth minute and Paulo Cesar Wanchope wasted an excellent chance eight minutes later for Costa Rica.
Elias Mentes increased the home team's lead in the 53rd minute, scoring with a powerful shot from a chance brilliantly created by playmaker Mauricio Cienfuegos.
Luis Arnitez reduced the deficit four minutes later and the 36,000 crowd in the Cuscutlan stadium had to endure a nerve-wracking last few minutes as the away team piled on the pressure.
El Salvador, with two World Cup appearances behind them, moved into third place in the group with four points from two games. They lead Costa Rica, who have played one more game, on goal difference.

Mexico top the six-team group with eight points from four games, followed by the United States with five points from four. Canada and Jamaica trail with two points each from three games and, with the top three teams qualifying for France next year, appear to be out of the race.
